5 million, expanding its cardiac monitoring portfolio across ambulatory, inpatient and remote care settings.

The transaction consists of $237.5 million in cash, funded from iRhythm’s balance sheet, and $50 million in iRhythm common stock. iRhythm will also provide VitalConnect with up to $30 million in interim working capital financing before the acquisition closes.

VitalConnect’s technology will complement iRhythm’s Zio platform, which provides long-term continuous electrocardiogram monitoring for detecting cardiac arrhythmias. The acquisition will add mobile cardiac telemetry (MCT), inpatient monitoring and broader physiological monitoring capabilities to iRhythm’s existing offering.

VitalConnect operates an FDA-cleared platform incorporating a 4-in-1 wearable biosensor designed for continuous monitoring for up to 30 days. The technology can track as many as 11 physiological parameters, enabling monitoring across inpatient, outpatient and hospital-to-home environments.

...

iRhythm expects the acquisition to contribute to its revenue growth rate beginning in 2027 while maintaining its targeted adjusted EBITDA margin of 15% for that year.

By incorporating VitalConnect’s monitoring capabilities into its existing infrastructure and commercial operations, iRhythm is extending its focus from ambulatory arrhythmia detection toward cardiac monitoring across multiple care settings.

## MaineHealth receives state approval to acquire York Hospital

MaineHealth received the approval of state regulators to acquire York Hospital, the system said in a news release.

The transaction, first announced in October, is slated to close Oct. 1, according to the release.

“York Hospital has shared publicly that it has faced significant financial headwinds in recent years as a result of workforce shortages, rising costs and reimbursement challenges,” a spokesperson for MaineHealth said Aug. 11.

Additional financial details were not disclosed.

Nonclinical, back-office roles at York Hospital will be impacted.
Affected employees will have the opportunity to apply for new roles under MaineHealth.

Portland, Maine-based MaineHealth has 10 hospitals, more than 2,000 providers and an estimated 24,000 staff members.

6 days ago

* * *

## Wellstar Health acquires Mountain Lakes Medical Center

Wellstar Health System has acquired Mountain Lakes Medical Center, the health system said Aug. 10.

Financial details were not disclosed. The two organizations reached an acquisition agreement in June.

Clayton, Georgia-based Wellstar Mountain Lakes Medical Center is a 25-bed, full-service acute-care hospital. Leadership at the facility remains the same and all employees were retained, a spokesperson for Wellstar Health System said.

With the acquisition, the Marietta, Georgia-based health system has 12 hospitals in its network, along with an estimated 35,000 staff members and more than 400 care sites.

7 days ago

* * *

## iRhythm plans to acquire VitalConnect for $287.5 million
iRhythm Holdings has entered a definitive agreement to acquire VitalConnect, the digital health company said in an Aug. 6 news release.

iRhythm plans to purchase the wearable technology company for an estimated $287.5 million, which will be a mix of an estimated $237.5 million in cash and $50 million in iRhythm stock, according to the release.

Additionally, iRhythm will provide up to $30 million in interim working capital financing for VitalConnect to fund operations as the deal moves toward closing.

The transaction is slated to close by the end of the year, pending regulatory approval.

# VitalConnect Acquisition Marks iRhythm’s Strategic Leap Beyond Ambulatory Cardiac Monitoring

iRhythm Holdings is making ambitious moves with its definitive agreement to acquire VitalConnect for $287.5 million—a deal set to reshape its position within the cardiac monitoring industry.
This transaction, split between $237.5 million in cash and $50 million in iRhythm stock, is more than a simple expansion: it’s a strategic pivot toward an integrated, end-to-end cardiac monitoring platform that spans from ambulatory settings all the way to hospital-to-home care.

## Transaction Immediately Broadens Product Portfolio and Market Reach

Upon closing, iRhythm’s portfolio will instantly expand, notably with the addition of VitalConnect’s FDA-cleared wearable biosensor platform. VitalConnect’s technology isn’t limited to just one cardiac monitoring modality—it features flexible, multi-vitals continuous monitoring capabilities, potentially covering up to 11 physiological parameters. This means that iRhythm will be positioned not only in the traditional ambulatory cardiac monitoring market but will also accelerate its entry into inpatient and remote care sectors—areas with rising demand and substantial growth prospects.

Importantly, the company maintains its commitment to a 15% adjusted EBITDA margin target for 2027, signaling operational confidence despite the sizable acquisition investment. This fiscal discipline could help fund future R&D and innovation without derailing margin expectations.

## Strategic Rationale: Broadened Addressable Market and Platform for Innovation

For investors and industry followers, the acquisition signals iRhythm’s broader ambitions: to command a leading role in connected cardiac care, from real-time hospital monitoring to home-based health management. By folding in VitalConnect’s capabilities—including up to 30-day monitoring, four-in-one device functionality, and live data look-in—iRhythm increases its flexibility to adapt as cardiac care migrates away from a “one-size-fits-all” model.

# iRhythm to buy VitalConnect for $287.5M after Street-beating Q2

August 6, 2026 By [Chris Newmarker](https://www.massdevice.com/author/cnewmarker/)

iRhythm Technologies logo [iRhythm](https://www.massdevice.com/tag/irhythm/) (Nasdaq: IRTC) announced today that it will acquire wearable biosensor and ambulatory cardiac monitoring tech company VitalConnect.

The news, along with Street-beating second-quarter results, sent IRTC shares up more than 2% to $130.75 apiece in after-hours trading.

iRhythm (San Francisco) said the size of the acquisition is $287.5 million — $237.5 million in cash from iRhythm’s balance sheet and roughly $50 million in iRhythm common stock.
